questions.question: Which of the following is not a way in which underground water reaches the surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Through evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Springs** are natural points of discharge where the **Water Table** intersects the ground surface, allowing **Groundwater** to flow out freely due to gravity or hydrostatic pressure. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Wells** are man-made structures created by digging or drilling into the **Saturated Zone** of the earth to access and extract water for various purposes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Tube wells** are specialized deep-bore systems that use a long pipe to reach deep **Aquifers**, employing mechanical pumps to lift water to the surface level. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation** is the physical process by which water changes from a liquid to a gaseous state and moves into the **Atmosphere**, representing a loss of water from the surface rather than a delivery method from underground. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrological Context**:

 
 
• **Aquifers**: These are underground layers of **Permeable Rock** or sediment (like sand and gravel) that contain and transmit **Groundwater**.
 
• **Infiltration**: The downward movement of water from the surface into the soil, which is the primary method of **Aquifer Recharge**.
 
• **Water Table**: The upper limit of the portion of the ground that is completely saturated with water; it can fluctuate based on **Precipitation** and extraction.
 
• **Capillary Action**: The movement of water through tiny spaces in the soil, which can bring moisture up to plant roots but is not a method for discharging large volumes of water.
 
• **Transpiration**: Part of the **Water Cycle** where plants absorb water from the soil and release it into the air as vapor.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originated in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form that originated in the Indian state of **Kerala** and is recognized as one of the eight primary Indian classical dances by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
 
• The term is derived from the words **Mohini**, referring to the mythical enchantress avatar of **Lord Vishnu**, and **Aattam**, which means movement or dance in **Malayalam**; thus, it literally translates to the **dance of the enchantress**.
 
• It is traditionally a **solo dance** performed by women, characterized by its graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions that follow the **Lasya** style (delicate and feminine).
 
• The dance is known for its circular movements and the **Atavakul** (basic steps), which avoid abrupt jerks, mimicking the gentle flow of the backwaters and the swaying of palm trees in **Kerala**.
 
• The repertoire of Mohiniyattam includes items like **Cholkettu**, **Jatiswaram**, **Varnam**, **Padam**, and **Tillana**, primarily set to **Sopana Sangeetham** music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Classical Dances and States:**

 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:** This state is the home of **Bharatanatyam**, a dance form renowned for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and sophisticated sign language based on **hand gestures (mudras)**.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** It is the origin of **Kuchipudi**, a dance-drama that involves both singing and dancing, traditionally performed by men but now dominated by female practitioners.
 
• **Kerala (Other forms):** Besides Mohiniyattam, Kerala is also famous for **Kathakali**, a highly stylized classical dance-drama known for its heavy make-up and elaborate costumes.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Mohiniyattam:**
 
 
• **Costume:** Dancers typically wear a white or off-white **Kasavu saree** with a bright **gold-toned brocade** border, symbolizing purity.
 
• **Music:** The lyrics are usually in **Manipravalam**, a literary mixture of **Sanskrit** and **Malayalam**.
 
• **Notable Exponents:** Legends such as **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma**, **Sunanda Nair**, and **Jayaprabha Menon** have significantly contributed to its revival and global popularity.

questions.question: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dawn to Sunset**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramadan** is the ninth month of the **Islamic lunar calendar** and is observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of **fasting**, prayer, and reflection.
 
• The act of fasting, known as **Sawm**, is one of the **Five Pillars of Islam**, which are the foundational acts of worship for believers.
 
• The duration of the daily fast begins at **Dawn** (the time of the **Fajr** prayer) and concludes at **Sunset** (the time of the **Maghrib** prayer).
 
• During these hours, individuals abstain from consuming food, drinking any liquids, smoking, and engaging in sexual relations to cultivate **self-discipline** and spiritual growth.
 
• The start and end of the fast are determined by the **local lunar sightings**, which is why the dates of **Ramadan** shift approximately 10 to 11 days earlier each year in the Gregorian calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suhoor**:

 
 
• This is the **pre-dawn meal** eaten before the first light of day appears and the fast begins.
 
• It is a vital part of the daily routine to maintain physical strength and is considered a **blessed practice** in Islamic tradition.
 
 
 
• **Iftar**:
 
 
• This is the meal used to **break the fast** immediately after the sun sets.
 
• Following the tradition of Prophet Muhammad, many Muslims break their fast with **dates** and water before performing the evening prayer.
 
 
 
• **Laylat al-Qadr**:
 
 
• Known as the **Night of Power**, it is believed to be the night when the **Quran** was first revealed to the Prophet.
 
• It occurs during the **last ten days** of **Ramadan** and is considered the holiest night of the year.
 
 
 
• **Eid al-Fitr**:
 
 
• This major **Islamic festival** marks the end of the month of **Ramadan** and the beginning of the next month, **Shawwal**.

questions.question: Which state's tribal groups like Santhals are known for vibrant music using flutes and drums?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhals** are one of the largest **Scheduled Tribes** in India, with their primary concentration in the state of **Jharkhand**, though they also reside in West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar.
 
• Music and dance are fundamental pillars of **Santhal identity**, characterized by communal participation during seasonal festivals such as **Sohrai** (harvest festival) and **Baha** (flower festival).
 
• The **Tiriyo**, a traditional **bamboo flute** with seven holes, is considered the most prestigious melodic instrument in Santhal music, often associated with shepherd life and romantic folklore.
 
• Rhythmic accompaniment is provided by a variety of **drums**, most notably the **Tumdak** (a two-headed earthen drum) and the **Tamak** (a large kettle drum made of metal or wood).
 
• Their musical compositions are deeply connected to the **natural environment**, agricultural cycles, and the **worship of Marang Buru** (the supreme deity) and other ancestral spirits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka**:

 
 
• Home to the **Soliga** and **Iruliga** tribes.
 
• Famous for the **Dollu Kunitha**, a high-energy drum dance, and the **Goravara Kunitha** associated with Lord Mailara Linga.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Features the **Siddi** tribe, known for the **Dhamal dance** which uses the **Musira** drum, reflecting African musical influences.
 
• The **Rathwa** tribe performs the **Gheria** dance using traditional percussion.
 
 
 
• **Manipur**:
 
 
• Known for the **Naga** and **Kuki-Chin** tribal groups.
 
• Traditional music involves the **Pena** (a string instrument) and various heavy wooden **drums** used during the **Hao-Laa** folk songs.

questions.question: Which Indian mission made India the first country to successfully reach Mars orbit in its maiden attempt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangalyaan (MOM)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mangalyaan**, also officially known as the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)**, was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **November 5, 2013**.
 
• The spacecraft was launched using the **PSLV-C25** rocket from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**.
 
• India scripted history on **September 24, 2014**, by successfully placing the spacecraft into **Mars orbit** on its **very first attempt**.
 
• With this achievement, **India** became the **first nation** in the world to reach Mars orbit in its **maiden attempt** and the **fourth space agency** globally to reach Mars after **Roscosmos**, **NASA**, and the **European Space Agency**.
 
• The mission was primarily a **technology demonstrator** designed to test the capability of the Indian space program to send a craft into **interplanetary orbit** and operate it autonomously.
 
• The mission carried five scientific instruments to study **Martian surface features**, **morphology**, **mineralogy**, and the **Martian atmosphere**, specifically looking for **methane**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandrayaan-1**:

 
 
• Launched in **October 2008**, it was India's first mission to the **Moon**.
 
• It played a crucial role in discovering **water molecules** (H₂O) and **hydroxyl** on the lunar surface.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-2**:
 
 
• Launched in **July 2019**, it aimed to explore the **Lunar South Pole**.
 
• It consisted of an **Orbiter**, a lander named **Vikram**, and a rover named **Pragyan**; while the lander crashed, the orbiter remains operational.
 
 
 
• **Aditya-L1**:
 
 
• Launched in **September 2023**, it is India's first dedicated mission to study the **Sun**.
 
• It is positioned at the **Lagrange Point 1 (L1)** to observe **solar activities** like **coronal mass ejections** and **solar winds**.
 
 
 
• **Cost-Effectiveness**: The **Mars Orbiter Mission** is world-renowned for being one of the most **economical** interplanetary missions, costing approximately **450 Crore INR** (roughly **74 million USD**).

questions.question: Which was the first Asian country to host the FIFA World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Korea, Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2002 FIFA World Cup** was the **17th edition** of the tournament and holds the distinction of being the first ever held in the **Asian continent**.
 
• It was the first **FIFA World Cup** to be **co-hosted** by two different nations, with **South Korea** and **Japan** sharing the organizational responsibilities.
 
• The tournament took place between **May 31** and **June 30, 2002**, featuring **32 teams** playing a total of **64 matches** across 20 venues.
 
• The hosting decision was finalized by the **FIFA Executive Committee** in **1996** to promote football in the **East Asian** region and acknowledge its growing economic and sporting influence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tournament Highlights:**

 
 
• **Brazil** won the championship, claiming their **fifth world title** by defeating **Germany** **2−0** in the final at the **International Stadium Yokohama**.
 
• **South Korea** made history by becoming the first **Asian** team to reach the **semi-finals**, eventually finishing in **fourth place**.
 
• The tournament introduced several iconic figures to the world stage, including **Ronaldo**, who won the **Golden Shoe**, and **Oliver Kahn**, who received the **Golden Ball**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Nations:**
 
 
• **China** participated in the **2002 World Cup** for the first time in its history but has never hosted the men's tournament; however, it did host the inaugural **FIFA Women's World Cup** in **1991**.
 
• **Qatar** became the second **Asian** nation to host the event in **2022**, marking the first time the **World Cup** was held in the **Middle East**.
 
• Nations like **Vietnam**, **Malaysia**, and **Myanmar** have hosted major regional events like the **SEA Games** and **AFC Asian Cup** group stages but have not yet hosted a **FIFA World Cup**.

questions.question: Where was the 3rd BRICS Summit held in 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanya, China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **3rd BRICS Summit** was held on **April 14, 2011**, in **Sanya**, located in the **Hainan** province of **China**.
 
• This summit was a landmark event as it was the first time **South Africa** participated as a full member, marking the official transition of the group from **BRIC** to **BRICS**.
 
• The meeting was hosted by **President Hu Jintao** and attended by leaders including **Dilma Rousseff** (Brazil), **Dmitry Medvedev** (Russia), **Manmohan Singh** (India), and **Jacob Zuma** (South Africa).
 
• The central theme of the summit was **'Vision for the Future: Prosperity through Cooperation'**, focusing on the global economic situation and international financial reforms.
 
• The summit resulted in the adoption of the **Sanya Declaration**, which called for a more representative **international monetary system** and enhanced cooperation among **emerging economies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moscow, Russia**:

 
 
• While the first-ever formal summit was held in **Yekaterinburg, Russia** (2009), Russia has hosted multiple subsequent meetings, including the **7th Summit** in **Ufa** (2015) and the **12th Summit** (2020) under its chairmanship.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi, India**:
 
 
• India hosted its first summit, the **4th BRICS Summit**, in **New Delhi** in **2012**, where the concept of the **New Development Bank (NDB)** was first proposed.
 
• The city also hosted the **13th BRICS Summit** virtually in **2021**.
 
 
 
• **Johannesburg, South Africa**:
 
 
• This city hosted the **10th BRICS Summit** in **2018** and the **15th BRICS Summit** in **2023**.
 
• The **2023 Johannesburg Summit** was historically significant for announcing the expansion of the bloc to include **six new member nations**.

questions.question: Oxygen is replenished in the atmosphere mainly by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the fundamental biological process by which **green plants**, **algae**, and **cyanobacteria** produce their own food using **sunlight**.
 
• During this process, plants absorb **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** and water (H₂O) from the environment and convert them into **glucose**.
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)** is released as a vital by-product into the atmosphere during the **photolysis of water** in the **thylakoid membranes** of **chloroplasts**.
 
• The overall chemical reaction can be summarized as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• This process is essential for maintaining the **Oxygen-Carbon Dioxide balance** in the Earth's **biosphere**, effectively replenishing the oxygen consumed by other life forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Respiration**:

 
 
• It is a metabolic process where living organisms consume **Oxygen** to break down **nutrients** and produce **ATP** (energy).
 
• This process results in the release of **CO₂**, thereby decreasing atmospheric oxygen levels.
 
 
 
• **Combustion**:
 
 
• A chemical reaction involving a fuel and an **oxidant** (oxygen) that produces heat and light.
 
• It **depletes oxygen** from the atmosphere and increases the concentration of **greenhouse gases**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Activities**:
 
 
• Large-scale operations and the burning of **fossil fuels** in factories consume massive quantities of **Oxygen**.
 
• These activities contribute to **air pollution** and **Global Warming** by disrupting the natural gas cycles.

questions.question: Which former Indian cricketers announced their retirements from Test cricket in quick succession in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohit Sharma & Virat Kohli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rohit Sharma** and **Virat Kohli**, two of India’s most decorated cricketers, are often associated with major retirement news in the **2024-2025** period due to their transition out of specific formats.
 
• The duo famously announced their retirements from **T20 Internationals (T20Is)** in quick succession on **June 29, 2024**, immediately after India won the **ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2024** in **Barbados**.
 
• While the question mentions **Test cricket** in **2025**, these players remained active for the **World Test Championship (WTC) 2023-25** cycle, with widespread speculation regarding their retirement from the longest format following the **WTC Final** in **June 2025**.
 
• **Virat Kohli** announced his **T20I** departure during the post-match presentation of the World Cup final, where he was named **Player of the Match** for his crucial 76 runs.
 
• **Rohit Sharma** confirmed his own retirement from the format during the post-match press conference, ending his career as the highest run-scorer in **T20I** history at that time and the most successful Indian T20I captain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sachin Tendulkar & Sourav Ganguly**:

 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar** retired from **Test cricket** in **November 2013** after playing his 200th match against the West Indies.
 
• **Sourav Ganguly** retired from all forms of international cricket in **2008** following a home series against Australia.
 
 
 
• **Rahul Dravid & MS Dhoni**:
 
 
• **Rahul Dravid** announced his retirement from **Test cricket** in **March 2012**.
 
• **MS Dhoni** retired from **Test cricket** with immediate effect in **December 2014** during India’s tour of Australia.
 
 
 
• **Shubman Gill**:
 
 
• As of **2025**, he is a primary top-order batter and was appointed as the **Vice-Captain** of the Indian limited-overs teams in **2024**, representing the future of the squad.

questions.question: Which Indian states were the theme states for the 38th Surajkund International Crafts Mela 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab and Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **38th Surajkund International Crafts Mela** is scheduled to be held in **February 2025** at **Surajkund, Faridabad**, in the state of **Haryana**.
 
• For the 2025 edition, the states of **Punjab and Haryana** have been designated as the **Theme States**, representing a joint celebration of the rich cultural and traditional heritage of the **North Indian** region.
 
• The selection of **Punjab and Haryana** as theme states aims to showcase the **Spirit of the Five Rivers** and the **Vibrant Haryanvi Culture** through traditional art forms, music, and dance.
 
• The fair provides a platform for artisans from these states to exhibit specialized crafts such as **Phulkari** embroidery, **Punjabi Juttis**, and traditional **Haryanvi Handlooms** to a global audience.
 
• The **Surajkund Mela** is officially recognized as the **largest crafts fair in the world**, significantly contributing to the promotion of **rural artisans** and **indigenous handicrafts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organizational Structure**:

 
 
• The event is organized by the **Surajkund Mela Authority** and **Haryana Tourism**.
 
• Collaborating partners include the Union Ministries of **Tourism**, **Textiles**, **Culture**, and **External Affairs**.
 
 
 
• **History and Evolution**:
 
 
• The Mela was first hosted in **1987** to promote traditional Indian handicrafts.
 
• It was upgraded to an **International Level** event in **2013**, inviting participation from various countries across **Africa**, **Europe**, and **Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Partner Nation Concept**:
 
 
• Alongside the **Theme State**, the Mela features a **Partner Nation** every year to foster international cultural exchange.
 
• For instance, in the **37th edition (2024)**, the **United Republic of Tanzania** served as the partner nation, while **Gujarat** was the theme state.

questions.question: Which region in India is prone to earthquakes and landslides?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himalayan region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayan region** is geologically the most unstable and active part of India due to the ongoing **tectonic collision** between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**. This convergence results in the accumulation of immense stress, which is released through frequent and high-magnitude **earthquakes**.
 
• According to the **Seismic Zoning Map** developed by the **Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)**, the entire Himalayan belt falls under **Zone V** (Very High Damage Risk Zone) and **Zone IV** (High Damage Risk Zone).
 
• The region consists of **young fold mountains** characterized by steep slopes, high relief, and fragile, unconsolidated sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. These physical features make the terrain highly susceptible to **gravity-induced mass movements** such as **landslides**, **rockfalls**, and **debris flows**.
 
• Heavy **monsoon rainfall**, sudden **cloudbursts**, and the melting of glaciers act as triggering factors, lubricating the loose soil and rock layers, which leads to frequent disasters in states like **Uttarakhand**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Arunachal Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plain**:

 
 
• Composed of deep **alluvial deposits**, it lies between the Himalayas and the plateau.
 
• While it experiences ground shaking from Himalayan seismic events, its flat topography makes the risk of **landslides** negligible.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:
 
 
• Recognized as one of the oldest and most stable landmasses (**Craton**) on Earth.
 
• It has lower seismic activity compared to the north, although major exceptions like the **1993 Latur earthquake** and **1967 Koyna earthquake** indicate internal faulting.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• These regions are primarily vulnerable to **hydro-meteorological disasters** such as **cyclones**, **storm surges**, and **tsunamis** (notably the 2004 event).
 
• The lack of significant elevation gradients prevents large-scale **landslide** activity.

questions.question: Which river flows through the Grand Canyon of India (Gandikota)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Penna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gandikota** is a small village situated on the right bank of the **Penna River** in the **Kadapa** district of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It is famously known as the **Grand Canyon of India** because of the spectacular gorge formed by the **Penna River** cutting through the **Erramala Hills**.
 
• The canyon features deep valleys and massive boulders of **red granite**, creating a landscape that resembles the **Grand Canyon** of the **Colorado River** in the **United States**.
 
• The historical **Gandikota Fort**, which dates back to the **12th century**, is strategically perched on the edge of this gorge, offering a majestic view of the river winding through the rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Penna River Details**:

 
 
• The **Penna River** (also known as **Pennar**) originates in the **Nandi Hills** of **Chikkaballapur** district in **Karnataka**.
 
• It flows through the states of **Karnataka** and **Andhra Pradesh** before reaching its mouth at the **Bay of Bengal** near **Nellore**.
 
• Its major tributaries include the **Jayamangali**, **Kunderu**, **Sagileru**, **Chitravathi**, and **Papagni** rivers.
 
 
 
• **Other Southern Rivers**:
 
 
• **Krishna**: One of the longest rivers in India, originating at **Mahabaleshwar** in **Maharashtra** and flowing through **Karnataka**, **Telangana**, and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• **Kaveri**: Rising in the **Brahmagiri Hills** of **Kodagu**, **Karnataka**, it is known as the **Ganges of the South**.
 
• **Godavari**: The **second-longest** river in India, it originates at **Trimbakeshwar** in **Maharashtra** and is often called **Dakshin Ganga**.

questions.question: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with a velocity perpendicular to the field. What is the nature of its motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Circular path**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Why was the Zabt system under Mughal Empire not implemented in provinces like Gujarat and Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inability to survey the land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zabt System**, also known as the **Bandobast System**, was a sophisticated land revenue assessment method introduced during the reign of **Mughal Emperor Akbar** around **1580-1582**.
 
• This system was primarily designed and implemented by Akbar's finance minister, **Raja Todar Mal**, and it relied heavily on the **Dahshala** principle, which averaged crop yields and prices over the previous **ten years**.
 
• A fundamental requirement for the **Zabt system** was the **measurement of land** and the maintenance of detailed **statistical records** regarding cultivation and productivity for each **Bigha** of land.
 
• In provinces like **Gujarat** and **Bengal**, the **Mughal administration** could not implement this system because they lacked the necessary administrative reach and historical data to perform accurate **land surveys**.
 
• The **geographic complexities** of the **Bengal delta** and the late integration of **Gujarat** into the central administrative fold made the **physical measurement** of every field logistically impossible at that time.
 
• Consequently, in these frontier or outlying provinces, the state reverted to older or less rigorous methods of revenue collection, such as **Nasaq** or **Kankut**, which did not require detailed annual **surveys**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poor soil quality**: This was not the reason for the exclusion; **Bengal** was one of the most fertile provinces of the **Mughal Empire**, known for its high **agricultural productivity** and **monsoon-fed** crops.
 
• **Frequent foreign invasions**: While the **Mughals** faced various regional challenges, the implementation of **Zabt** was hindered more by **internal administrative logistics** and **geography** than by external military threats.
 
• **Lack of local administration**: While **Bengal** and **Gujarat** had strong local **Zamindari** systems, the specific failure was the **technical inability** to conduct **Paimash** (measurement), which was the core pillar of the **Zabt** revenue model.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal**: Apart from the **Zabt system**, he is credited with introducing standardized units of measurement like the **Gaz-i-Ilahi** and classifying land into four categories: **Polaj**, **Parauti**, **Chachar**, and **Banjar**.

questions.question: In India, the new National Sports Policy 2025 supersedes the existing _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Sports Policy 2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Sports Policy 2025** is a comprehensive framework formulated by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to modernize the sporting ecosystem in India and align it with the vision of **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**.
 
• This policy officially supersedes the **National Sports Policy 2001**, which had been the primary document guiding sports development in the country for nearly 24 years.
 
• While the 2001 policy focused on the dual objectives of **Broad-basing of Sports** and **Achieving Excellence in Sports** at the national and international levels, the 2025 policy expands this scope to include **Sports Science**, **Digital Transformation**, and **Sustainable Sports Infrastructure**.
 
• The 2025 framework aims to strengthen the **National Sports Federations (NSFs)** through better **governance** and **transparency**, moving away from the older administrative models established under the 2001 guidelines.
 
• It prioritizes the integration of sports into the **educational curriculum** and emphasizes the development of **high-performance centers** to prepare athletes for global events like the **2036 Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Sports Policy 2001**:

 
 
• It was the second major sports policy in India, replacing the **National Sports Policy 1984**.
 
• It introduced the concept of **incentives for sportspersons** and sought to involve **industrial houses** and the **private sector** in sports promotion.
 
• The policy led to the expansion of the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and focused on identifying talent at a young age.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Policy 1984**:
 
 
• This was the first formal sports policy of India, formulated following the successful hosting of the **1982 Asian Games** in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Khelo India Programme**:
 
 
• Launched in **2018**, this scheme serves as a functional arm to achieve the grassroots objectives outlined in the broader national policies by funding **talent identification** and **infrastructure development**.

questions.question: In the Union Budget 2025-26 announcement, which state has been chosen for establishing the Makhana Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025-26**, Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** announced the establishment of a dedicated **Makhana Board** in the state of **Bihar**.
 
• The primary objective of setting up this board is to promote the **cultivation**, **processing**, and **value addition** of Makhana, ensuring better price realization for farmers.
 
• **Bihar** accounts for more than **80 percent** of the total **Makhana** (fox nut) production in India and is the largest producer globally, particularly in the **Mithila region**.
 
• The board will facilitate **scientific research**, provide training to farmers, and establish **quality control mechanisms** to enhance the export competitiveness of Indian Makhana in international markets.
 
• This move is part of the central government’s strategy to strengthen **agricultural infrastructure** and promote regional specialty crops as part of the **vocal for local** initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mithila Makhana GI Tag**:

 
 
• In August 2022, **Mithila Makhana** was granted the **Geographical Indication (GI) Tag**, ensuring that only the makhana produced in this specific region of **Bihar** can use the name.
 
• Key producing districts in Bihar include **Darbhanga**, **Madhubani**, **Purnia**, **Katihar**, and **Sitaram-Supaul**.
 
 
 
• **Nutritional Significance**:
 
 
• Known as a **superfood**, Makhana is rich in **protein**, **calcium**, and **magnesium** while being extremely low in **saturated fats** and **sodium**.
 
• It is increasingly popular in the **wellness industry** as a healthy gluten-free snack alternative.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**:
 
 
• The **Makhana Board** is expected to generate significant employment in **rural Bihar** and reduce the role of middlemen through organized **marketing cooperatives**.

questions.question: In tennis, when a player reduces the speed of his shot to land the ball just above the net and onto the opposite side, it is called a _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drop shot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Drop shot** is a delicate **touch shot** in tennis played with the intention of making the ball land just over the net, as close to the net as possible on the opponent's side.
 
• The shot is executed by reducing the speed of the racquet at the moment of impact, often using a **Continental grip** to provide better control and feel.
 
• The primary mechanical feature of a drop shot is the application of **backspin** or **underspin**, which causes the ball to lose its forward momentum and 'die' or bounce vertically upon hitting the court surface.
 
• Tactically, it is used to exploit an opponent who is positioned deep behind the **baseline**, forcing them to move rapidly forward to reach the ball before it bounces twice.
 
• Elite players like **Roger Federer** and **Novak Djokovic** are known for using the drop shot as a **deception tool**, disguising the motion to look like a standard heavy groundstroke until the last millisecond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smash**:

 
 
• A powerful **overhead stroke** hit with a motion similar to a serve, usually in response to a high **lob**.
 
• It is designed to be a **point-winning shot** by directing the ball downward at high velocity into the opponent's court.
 
 
 
• **Slice**:
 
 
• A technique where the racquet strings brush underneath the ball to create **underspin**.
 
• While the drop shot is a type of slice, a standard **slice groundstroke** travels deep into the court and stays low to the ground after the bounce, making it difficult for opponents to generate power.
 
 
 
• **Two-hand**:
 
 
• This refers to the **two-handed backhand**, a popular stroke where the player uses both hands on the racquet handle.
 
• It provides increased **stability** and **leverage**, allowing players to handle high-velocity balls and **topspin** more effectively than a one-handed backhand.
